reviews.text: Hi, Virai. We are sorry to hear that we didn’t meet your expectation. We have very high expectations at GoodVets West Loop and would love the opportunity to improve. Please get in touch with us at (312) 548-9588!
Hi, Elizabeth. Thank you so much for rating your experience with us so highly!
Perfect , loved that I could drop her off

Took my puppy in to get her vaccinations up to date and the doctor gave her the wrong vaccine. Then had to give her an allergy shot for it. What’s worse is, she didn’t take ownership or even apologize for it. Instead she  presented it as a “gift”, stating I wouldn’t be charged and then made a joke about now would be the time to take my puppy out because she was given this additional vaccine. After I spoke with management, I decided to stay with this facility as long as this doctor would never care for my puppy again. However, I’ve seen two doctors since and they are both fairly new to practice. I found myself going back a third time because my puppy’s issues are not getting better. Might be time to move on to a different provider with seasoned doctors.

Didn’t help my cat simply because they just didn’t want to or didn’t know how. Similar to the other reviews, they just gave him the vaccines (while he was weak and sick), told us to pick him up in couple hours, we came back and learned that they couldn’t help except telling us to take him to ER and still charged $800. Thank goodness our cat was helped by the ER team (expensive but worth it) and his regular vet. Front desk staff is probably the only good part at this clinic. Really wanted to like these people but definitely don’t think we could recommend as we genuinely believe they don’t really care about you or your pets.
My first went well. The staff were friendly and informative. Most importantly, I did not feel pressured to purchase anything.
I Liked the experience. Almost everyone was nice and attentive. Very pricey, but they helped my cat. That's all I care about.
Great experience, been coming here for years. They have all 3 of our pets' profiles and know them well, regardless of which vet is seeing them.
Do not take your Pets to this place ... All they care about is Money.

They keep scheduling appointments for my dog that I did not schedule, this is an ongoing problem that they won't address. It's been well over a year since we visited this office and every few months I get a random text telling me that I have to confirm an appointment that I never made. Each time I tell them to stop doing this and please don't schedule more appointments without permission. Nobody has ever responded, and then they do it again. Private equity vets suck and at this point I just want to be left alone.
Hi, Roshell.  Thank you so much for your kind review and trust with your furry family member. We look forward to seeing you both again soon!

I took my dog to GoodVets West Loop for an urgent, painful issue—an impacted and infected anal gland—and it resulted in the single worst veterinary experience I’ve had in five years of owning him. After digging into it, it’s clear why this place is run so terribly: GoodVets is backed by private equity firms (like General Atlantic), and they are blatantly putting corporate profits and daily volume over pet welfare.
Day 1: Wrong Charts and Understaffing
We had a 4:00 PM appointment on Tuesday, August 25th. Before going in, I gave him 150 mg of Trazodone as prescribed for his vet anxiety. During the exam, Dr. Fournier started reading off chart notes that didn't apply to my dog at all, blithely blaming a colleague for leaving "bad notes."
They took him to the back, only to return him 45 minutes later completely untreated. The reason? They were so understaffed they couldn't get enough hands to hold him down. Their "solution" was to tell me to bring him back the next morning, but instructed me to megadose him with 300 mg of Trazodone early in the morning and drop him off at 7:30 AM for an 8:00 AM appointment.
Day 2: 12 Hours Held Hostage While Heavy Sedation Wore Off
I followed their instructions and dropped him off at 7:30 AM on Wednesday. By 12:00 PM, having heard nothing, I called. The front desk claimed he was "resting comfortably," but when I forced her to check if he’d actually been seen, she admitted he hadn't even been examined yet.
I demanded a call from management. Two hours later, the Lead Veterinarian called and tried to gaslight me, claiming I only had a "floating appointment." I referenced my written treatment plan from the day before explicitly listing an 8:00 AM appointment. My dog sat in a cage for over seven hours while a massive dose of sedation completely wore off, leaving him terrified and in pain before they even touched him. She had zero answer for why they had me heavily drug him just to let him sit there all day.
He wasn't examined until after 5:00 PM—over nine hours past his appointment.
By 7:30 PM—12 full hours after drop-off—I still had no call, so I went to the clinic. The front desk worker claimed she tried calling me, but my phone log proved that was a lie. When I demanded the contact info for the owner or manager, the front desk and the back-of-house staff claimed nobody knew who owned the practice and suggested I "just Google it."
This place is run like a cold, corporate factory. They overbook, understaff, waste heavy medication, and leave suffering animals in kennels for 12 hours to hit profit metrics, all while shielding ownership behind a wall of deliberate ignorance. Do not trust GoodVets with your pets.
They quoted me $198 for a radiograph consult in the examining room, and that price magically ballooned 2.5x when I got to the counter to pay: $506. Go elsewhere.
Hi, Sarah. Thank you so much for rating your experience with us so highly!
Hi, Laruby. We are delighted that you had a great experience with us. Thank you for trusting us with your pet!

I brought my dog to GoodVets West Loop to treat a few different issues, including skin lesions on his body, a torn claw, and an ear infection. The ear infection was the only thing they actually managed to solve.
For his other issues, they sent us home with and administered a massive list of treatments: **Simplicef** (antibiotic tablets), **DouxoS3 PYO Mousse**, **Animax Ointment**, a **Cytopoint injection** for allergies, and a **cone** to prevent him from scratching, biting, and itching himself.
As soon as I started giving him the prescribed medicine exactly as instructed, he suddenly started bleeding from his penis.
When I brought this up, they had me bring in a urine sample. That test came back clean. Next, they told me we needed to do an X-ray and blood work to figure out what was going on. I agreed to start with the X-ray, which thankfully also came back clean.
I was fully planning on moving forward with the recommended blood work next—until I saw what they were trying to charge me. They had originally given me an estimate of $187 for the X-ray, but then tried to charge me over $500 for it.
Between the prescribed medicine immediately causing him to bleed, and the clinic trying to sneak in a massive $500 charge for an X-ray they estimated at $187, I completely lost trust in this place. I will not be returning.

Despite all the reviews that I seen I tried to give this place a shot and I got burned
We love good vets! Always the best care when we visit. Thanks for all they do for our pets. ❤️

When I tell you to RUN from this place, I sincerely mean it. They do not care about your beloved pets, they just want to gaslight and fear monger pet owners so they can scam them.

My first experience at this Good Vets location was because my dog was squinting and his eye looked a little swollen. He has had a corneal abrasion in the past from rubbing his face, so I called and brought him in that day. He had his annual exam seven months prior at the GV in Nashville, but their systems aren't linked, so I had all of his records sent over. When presented the estimate, there was a heart worm test that he JUST had done and bloodwork that was never discussed. When I confronted the vet, she claimed it was sometimes hard to read the chart....? Isn't that a CRUCIAL part of the job? After removing those, it brought my estimate from $900 down to less than $400. I opted for a full ocular exam (a whole series of tests) because she gaslit me into thinking it could be something serious due to his age. After my dog passed every test, she shrugged it off as allergies. While waiting to pay, the RUDEST front desk woman goes "can I help you?" Yes obviously. I also asked for a full year of Simparica Trio because we were out and again they told me I needed a heart worm test otherwise they could only give me a four month supply. I pushed back, so they gave it to me. $750

Three weeks ago, my dog was showing symptoms of a UTI. They won't let you bring a sample because its "not sterile," so they insisted they had to do an ultrasound guided urinalysis. I asked how much that would be and the tech told me $184, so I agreed. The base charge for the office visit is $102, so in my head I was like alright under $300 fine. I go to pay and the front desk woman tells me its right under $500. I go uhh how did we get to $500? she goes "I'll e-mail you an itemized receipt." NO you're going to read it out loud BEFORE I pay... She reluctantly rattles everything off and it turns out the urine retrieval was $184 but the actual urinalysis is $60 more. Then the antibiotics were $77 plus the $102 office visit but THEN they charged me an extra $60 or so for a "senior exam" I was like well the fact that I don't even know what that consists of means I didn't consent to it and she was like oh you didn't do that today? Ok I'll take it off. $425 for a UTI.

We finished his prescription a week ago, two weeks 2x per day, and now his symptoms are back in full force. I call GV WL and ask for more or different antibiotics as it was obviously not resolved. She tells me they "can't just write prescriptions" and I'd have to bring him back in for more testing. I was like I am NOT giving you guys another $425 just to get more medicine when we were just there and you did a thorough exam. She's like ok I'll note that you're refusing an exam and see if the doctor can extend the prescription and have her call you back. No call back.

So, I call a vet that we haven't been to in over a decade and see if they can get us in. They tell me to BRING a sample. I was like oh ok if I don't get one do you guys do an ultrasound guided urinalysis? She says no, you'll just walk him outside and collect one. Ok great, and how much is the urinalysis? $55. The office visit is $45 (Good Vets is $102). If I would have gone there in the first place it would have been $100 (plus the antibiotic price) vs. $425 at Good Vets (plus if I had brought him back in and paid another $425!?!).

I'm also concerned that if he's having reoccurring UTI's he might have bladder stones. Which, if Good Vets actually did the ultrasound wouldn't they have seen that? I'm very concerned as to why two full weeks of antibiotics did not clear this up, and if a UTI goes untreated it can spread to the kidneys and potentially become fatal. We will never return to this Good Vets location as they only care about money and pushing unnecessary tests rather than getting your pet healthy. I don't have time for Good Vets' negligence.

If you love your pet(s), this is not the vet for you.
